DisplayName: Architecture decision governance and ADR stewardship
Summary: Guide architecture decisions from intake through option analysis, governance review, approval, and downstream rollout guidance without losing domain accountability or reusable evidence.
ValueStatement: Improve decision quality and prevent repeated architectural churn by forcing explicit options, trade-offs, approval reasoning, and follow-up obligations into durable ADR-style records.
InterfaceContractSummary: Decision demand, domain context, system constraints, and change risks are transformed into a reviewable architecture decision record with named owners and adoption conditions.
GovernanceNotes: Architecture decisions are treated as operating contracts, not slideware. The process requires evidence, option comparison, and explicit domain-owner participation.
ChangeSummary: Merged from SAMM governance, SSDF preparation and design, and lightweight ADR discipline so the process stays reusable across product, platform, and AI-oriented decisions.
GovernancePolicySummary: No architecture decision may be accepted without explicit context, considered options, decision rationale, risk notes, and named adoption obligations.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: The board may delay decisions, but cannot hide uncertainty by approving vague direction that nobody owns.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with human approval. Analysis may be AI-assisted, but acceptance and organizational commitment stay human.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Good fit for decision-board rehearsal, architecture review automation, and portfolio-level consistency analysis.
Metrics: Percentage of decisions with explicit adoption owners
Number of decisions with unresolved security or compliance follow-ups
Risks: Domain owners are missing and decisions become detached from operational reality.
The board approves direction without concrete trade-off evidence.
Security/compliance concerns are added too late to influence the actual decision.
Decisions are written but not translated into rollout guidance.
TailoringRules: For low-risk local decisions, merge governance review and approval into one step if domain-owner coverage remains explicit.
For AI or data-sensitive architecture changes, make compliance-steward review mandatory.
For cross-team platform decisions, add linked rollout work items after approval.

Steps.Title: Capture architecture decision demand
Steps.Subtitle: Define the decision boundary and why now
Steps.Notes: Normalize the incoming design tension into a single decision problem statement with scope, urgency, and impacted domains.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Design concern, change proposal, incident learning, or product demand requiring architecture direction.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Typed decision intake with named context owner and impacted domains.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Decision intake brief and initial affected-system list.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Governance facilitator may reject vague requests that do not define a real decision.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not proceed when scope and affected domains are not explicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Facilitation remains with trained board coordinator.
A domain owner must review the intake boundary.

Steps.Title: Assemble context, constraints, and options
Steps.Subtitle: Evidence before preference
Steps.Notes: Collect current-state constraints, target outcomes, option set, and measurable trade-offs before the board debates a preferred answer.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Decision intake, current system context, risk drivers, and domain constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: ADR draft with options, trade-offs, and recommendation.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Draft ADR and supporting context evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect authors the option analysis; domain owner confirms local reality and adoption cost.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If fewer than two meaningful options are considered, explain why explicitly.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Product value trade-offs are reviewed before board discussion.

Steps.Title: Review security, compliance, and policy impact
Steps.Subtitle: Decision quality includes control impact
Steps.Notes: Evaluate whether the proposed options change data exposure, trust assumptions, regulatory boundaries, or operational policy obligations.
Steps.InputContractSummary: ADR draft, system context, data flows, control inventory, and third-party implications.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Review note covering security and policy implications.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security and compliance findings tied to decision options.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer and compliance steward may force rework when controls are under-specified.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No approval when control obligations are ambiguous.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Compliance review becomes required for regulated domains.
Service owner reviews operational control impact.

Steps.Title: Make the board decision and record rationale
Steps.Subtitle: Approval is a commitment, not just agreement
Steps.Notes: Approve, defer, or reject the recommended architecture direction with explicit rationale, dissent notes, and adoption conditions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Reviewed ADR draft, option analysis, and security/compliance notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or deferred architecture decision with adoption conditions.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Board decision record and named follow-up obligations.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Governance facilitator records the decision; service owner and domain owner must both acknowledge adoption obligations.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not approve with placeholders for ownership or decision rationale.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Approved
BranchOutcomes.Description: The ADR is accepted with adoption conditions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Deferred
BranchOutcomes.Description: The ADR requires more evidence or narrower scope.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Operational decision approval remains with accountable owner.

Steps.Title: Publish rollout guidance and revisit triggers
Steps.Subtitle: Translate decision into executable downstream expectations
Steps.Notes: Turn the approved ADR into rollout guidance, architectural guardrails, and explicit revisit triggers so implementation teams know how to apply the decision.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Published rollout guidance and revisit criteria.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Architecture guidance note and future revisit triggers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect owns technical guidance; governance facilitator ensures revisit criteria are durable.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If rollout expectations cannot be stated clearly, the decision is not ready for downstream implementation.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture guidance ownership remains with the architect.

LocalRoles.Summary: Business-technical steward for a bounded domain affected by architectural change.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Represent domain semantics, operational realities, and long-term consequences when architecture choices affect a specific capability area.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A leader who understands the domain model deeply enough to challenge superficially convenient architecture decisions.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Business-technical steward for a bounded domain affected by architectural change.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior domain lead or engineering manager
KnowledgeRequirements: Deep knowledge of the owned domain’s rules, invariants, operational pain points, and integration surface.
Ability to evaluate whether an architectural proposal preserves domain boundaries and team ownership clarity.
Understanding of business impact if domain semantics are oversimplified or coupled incorrectly.
Knowledge of historical debt or prior incidents tied to domain boundary mistakes.
Ability to distinguish local optimization from portfolio-level harm.
Understanding of how the domain evolves and where future change cost is likely to land.
ExperienceRequirements: Has owned delivery or operations for a specific product domain over time.
Has corrected or challenged architecture choices that harmed domain clarity.
Has reviewed cross-team changes touching owned domain boundaries.
Has captured domain-specific lessons after incidents or major changes.
Has aligned domain stakeholders on non-obvious architectural trade-offs.
DecisionRights: Approve or challenge architectural impact on the owned domain.
Require an ADR when domain boundary or ownership is materially affected.
Escalate cross-domain coupling risk before implementation begins.
Demand clear ownership and migration planning for affected domain responsibilities.
CollaborationExpectations: Collaborate with architect, product owner, and engineers.
Contribute historical context without blocking needed evolution.
Ensure downstream domain teams understand changes affecting them.
Capture domain-specific follow-up actions after a decision.
AntiPatterns: Defending the current domain shape as sacred regardless of evidence.
Ignoring future ownership ambiguity because the short-term change works.
Withholding domain context until late design review.
Approving architecture without considering team-operability consequences.
FitnessEvidence: Domain impact notes accepted by architecture review.
Reduced domain-coupling surprises after decisions involving the role holder.
Evidence of better architectural continuity across releases.

LocalRoles.Summary: Facilitator for architecture decision workflow discipline, records, and follow-through.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Keep architecture governance lightweight but rigorous by ensuring the right decision, evidence, and follow-up happen at the right time.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A governance-capable facilitator who understands enough architecture to structure the process without dominating the decision.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Facilitator for architecture decision workflow discipline, records, and follow-through.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior PMO, architecture operations, or governance lead
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to structure review cadence, decision input, and follow-up tracking for architecture forums.
Knowledge of what makes an ADR or design decision truly decision-ready.
Understanding of stakeholder alignment patterns and unresolved-risk escalation.
Ability to detect when discussion is circling without explicit decision framing.
Knowledge of traceability and retention needs for governance artifacts.
Ability to keep governance proportional to the cost of the decision.
ExperienceRequirements: Has facilitated design or governance forums with multiple stakeholders.
Has maintained ADR or design review pipelines and follow-up tracking.
Has converted vague design discussion into explicit decision outcomes.
Has pushed incomplete proposals back for refinement without adding bureaucracy.
Has closed the loop on architecture action items after review.
DecisionRights: Decide whether a proposal is ready for formal review.
Require decision record completeness and explicit action ownership.
Escalate when architecture risk is unresolved but implementation pressure is mounting.
Define the minimal review footprint for low versus high impact decisions.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate between architects, domain owners, and delivery managers.
Keep review participants aligned on the current question and exit criteria.
Preserve decision records and action traces cleanly.
Improve the governance loop based on repeated friction patterns.
AntiPatterns: Turning every design question into a heavyweight forum item.
Allowing review meetings to end without a decision or owned next step.
Confusing facilitation authority with design authority.
Treating documentation as the outcome instead of the decision.
FitnessEvidence: Governance records with clear outcomes and owners.
Reduced decision drift or repeated review loops.
Stakeholder trust in review readiness signals.
Action closure rates after facilitated governance sessions.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Decision-prep brief that frames the architecture question, options, and decision deadline before a formal ADR is finalized.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for the current decision cycle and later governance context only.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must make the decision question explicit, not only the desired answer.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Checks whether an architecture proposal is mature enough for a governance decision.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: A proposal is about to enter formal architecture governance.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Decision participants can answer the core question with evidence instead of re-discovering context live.
Checks: Relevant domain owners were consulted or intentionally not needed.
Implementation pressure or deadline is visible.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms the impacted domain owners have been consulted before a cross-domain decision is locked in.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Every materially affected domain has either participated or been explicitly waived with rationale.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Architecture decision is proceeding with hidden affected domains or ownership blind spots.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate to architecture facilitator and chief architect before approval.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for rewriting fuzzy design debates into crisp decision questions.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to collapse materially different options into one fake choice.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Represent live-service constraints, operational history, and post-release accountability in change decisions.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A domain-aligned owner with authority over service-level objectives, support load, and operational trade-offs.
RoleUsages.Notes: Operational accountability owner for a live service, product surface, or bounded business capability.
